## Organizational deployment and sustained governance

Source basis: [Slow AI Kitchen](https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) · [GRC Workbook](https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)

| **Canonical step** | **Required capability** | **Workbook records** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 Plan the Menu | Gate 8: authorized tools, permitted workflows, task tiers and deployment policy. | W05, W06, W07, W10 |
| 11 Staff the Brigade | Gate 9: competent, authorized operators and an escalation chain reaching an executive. | W04, W22 |
| 12 Run the Event | Gate 10: operational audit and review, incidents, corrective action and registry revision. | W14, W18 to W21, W24 |

Steps 10 to 12 apply to organizational use at every task risk tier. A low-risk drafting task still needs approved tools and capable operators. Registry status, task release and the day-30 expansion decision are separate records.

**The operating cycle**

Use LEARN for context and stakeholders; ALIGN for objectives, tolerances and responses; PERFORM for controls, training and response; REVIEW for evidence and improvement. Feed learning back into the cycle.

**The institutional program**

The Kitchen addendum identifies five continuing pillars: Governance Structure, Risk Management Framework, Regulatory Compliance, AI Lifecycle Management and Continuous Improvement. Assign continuing owners and gaps in W24.

Slow AI: AI that cannot be governed, explained and audited is not deployed; the three tests are conjunctive, and the doctrine is a precondition, not a speed limit. Informed Intent: no AI system acts without prior authorization stating its purpose, authority, boundaries and exit, given by a human who meets the five authorizer conditions. Final Liability rests with the Human: every material outcome attaches to a named human owner with decision rights, oversight and the power to intervene. The normative statement of the three doctrines is [DOCTRINE.md](https://github.com/rolldabones/rolldabones/blob/main/DOCTRINE.md); this workbook adds instruments, not doctrine.
